title: The information environment is becoming a platform-accountability, trust, and research-capacity problem
source_unit: International Panel on the Information Environment, Trends in the Information Environment: 2026 Expert Survey Results
geography: Global expert survey covering 71 countries, with separate USA, developing-economy, and other-developed-economy comparisons

observations.period: May–June 2026; expert outlook on information-environment direction

denominator.unit: experts studying the information environment across 71 countries

expected_deterioration.unit: percent expecting the information environment in their country of expertise to worsen over the coming year

deterioration_trend.value: 76% in 2026 versus 53% in 2023, 63% in 2024, and 72% in 2025; the latest increase is within sampling variation

expert_pessimism_mechanism.value: Information-environment risk is experienced as a combined platform, trust, political-pressure, and knowledge-production problem

observations.method: Fourth annual IPIE expert survey, fielded May 6–June 8, 2026; respondents were recruited through academic databases, professional networks, and nominations rather than probability sampling.
observations.uncertainty: This is an expert-judgment panel, not a probability sample of experts or the public. Waves are similar but not identical, and perceived deterioration is not a direct behavioral or content-quality measure.
observations.subgroup: Experts studying developing economies, the USA, and other developed economies; the report separately analyzes these groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Rising pessimism may reflect greater awareness, changing sample composition, or salience of political events rather than a uniform deterioration in every information system.

observations.period: May–June 2026; platform power, misinformation, polarization, and information trust

denominator.unit: IPIE experts; threat ratings refer to respondents' main country of expertise

platform_accountability_threat.unit: percent rating lack of platform accountability a big or extreme threat

misinformation_threat.unit: percent rating misinformation a big or extreme threat

polarization_threat.unit: percent rating polarization a big or extreme threat

findability_trust_gap.value: 76% say diverse viewpoints are at least somewhat easy to find online, but only 28% think most people trust mainstream news to report politics accurately

platform_legitimacy_mechanism.value: Access to viewpoints does not automatically produce trusted, accurate, or civically usable information

observations.method: Expert ratings of information-environment threats and public access/trust conditions.
observations.uncertainty: Experts assess their country of expertise and may differ in topic, region, and professional standpoint; the findings do not estimate public exposure or causally rank threat effects.
observations.subgroup: Global experts, with stronger threat ratings among developing-economy and USA experts than among other developed-economy experts on several measures.
observations.counterinterpretation: High viewpoint availability may be a sign of pluralism rather than dysfunction; low trust can reflect partisan media judgments, institutional history, or broader political conflict.

observations.period: May–June 2026; AI summaries in search and the intermediary-to-source trade-off

denominator.unit: IPIE experts; AI-summary questions asked in the 2026 survey wave

ai_summary_speed.unit: percent expecting AI search summaries to help people find answers faster

ai_summary_news_traffic.unit: percent expecting AI summaries to reduce visits to news websites

ai_summary_viewpoint_diversity.unit: percent expecting AI summaries to narrow the viewpoints users encounter

intermediary_mechanism.value: Convenience and speed can rise while source visibility, direct audience ownership, and exposure diversity weaken

observations.method: New 2026 expert-survey questions on AI summaries in search engines, alongside broader technology-effect ratings.
observations.uncertainty: These are forecasts from experts, not observed traffic or viewpoint-diversity outcomes; the survey does not identify which search products, markets, or news organizations would be affected.
observations.subgroup: Experts studying information environments across global regions; USA and developing-economy experts report distinct threat and research-pressure profiles.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI summaries could increase access for people who otherwise would not reach information, and faster answers may improve practical agency even if click-through falls.

observations.period: May–June 2026; research capacity, political pressure, and public-knowledge infrastructure

denominator.unit: IPIE experts; barrier percentages are calculated over all respondents and multiple responses were allowed

funding_barrier.unit: percent citing research funding as a barrier

data_access_barrier.unit: percent citing restricted data access as a barrier

government_agenda_pressure.unit: percent reporting pressure to align research with a government political agenda

government_censorship.unit: percent reporting government censorship of their research

knowledge_capacity_mechanism.value: The capacity to measure and contest information harms is itself exposed to funding, data, censorship, surveillance, and political-alignment pressures

observations.method: Multiple-response questions on research barriers and pressures in the 2026 expert survey; comparisons are made with prior waves.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported professional pressures are not independently audited; cross-wave comparisons reflect changing samples and question wording where noted.
observations.subgroup: USA experts report government funding control and political-alignment pressure at higher rates than experts elsewhere; country-of-expertise groups are not population estimates.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reporting a barrier does not establish research suppression, publication bias, or a measurable decline in public information quality, though it identifies a plausible capacity risk.

related_sources.claim: IPIE Summary for Policymakers provides a concise account of AI-summary trade-offs, platform accountability, research pressure, and global expert sampling.
IPIE press release corroborates the 470-expert, 71-country sample, deterioration outlook, platform threat, trust gap, and research-pressure findings.

boundary: This record is expert-assessment evidence about the global information environment and the capacity to study it. It does not establish public-level exposure, platform causality, observed news traffic, actual censorship rates, public trust trends, or the effects of AI summaries on civic participation.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official IPIE 2026 synthesis-report page reviewed for sample, field dates, threat estimates, AI-summary trade-offs, research barriers, subgroup comparisons, and sampling limitations.
reproduction_audit.version_note: The report page includes the survey summary and full report text; the associated questionnaire and replication data should be used for exact subgroup or wave-level reproduction.
